proposal: The Mandate recommends that BIS act unilaterally to tighten Export Administration Regulations for countries of concern such as China and Russia, reversing 2008 to 2016 loosening. Listed steps include moving toward more restrictive country groups, ending license exceptions, broadening foreign direct product rules, lowering the de minimis threshold, tightening deemed-export and fundamental-research rules, adding many more companies to the Entity List, and denying licenses where end-use checks are blocked.
remaining: Decide whether the affiliates rule resumes on 2026-11-10 or is extended; a commentary page reported announced extension plans to 2027-01-10 but no Federal Register extension as of 2026-10-03.

Rules on de minimis thresholds, foreign direct product reach, deemed exports, fundamental research, license exceptions and 'specially designed' items: no action found in BIS Federal Register documents since 2025-01-20.
Redesignation of China and Russia to more restrictive country groups: no action found.

Open nomination process for emerging and foundational technology controls, equal agency votes in license disputes, and quarterly license data to Congress: no related BIS document found in the Federal Register review (not exhaustively checked).

Entity List treatment of apps such as TikTok and WeChat: a Federal Register search of BIS documents for those names since 2025-01-20 returned nothing. A Justice Department rule on restricting bulk data transfers to countries of concern (published 2025-01-08 under Executive Order 14117) is a parallel measure of different design, not the BIS-implemented executive order the Mandate describes.

status_summary: BIS has issued rules in both directions. Tightening steps include large Entity List additions in 2025 (two rules on 2025-03-28 covering about 80 entities, most under China; 30 entities on 2025-09-16, 23 of them under China; 26 entities and 3 addresses on 2025-10-09), removal of validated end-user status for three China chip plants (effective 2025-12-31), and a 2025-09-30 rule extending Entity List restrictions to entities 50 percent or more owned by listed parties. That affiliates rule has been suspended since 2025-11-10 as part of a U.S.-China trade arrangement announced by the White House on 2025-11-01; the suspension runs through 2026-11-09, and no extension had appeared in the Federal Register by early October 2026. Loosening steps include a 2026-01-15 rule moving licenses for certain advanced AI chips to China and Macau from presumed denial to case-by-case review and an August 2026 rule easing controls on drones with under three hours of endurance. BIS's Entity List rules in 2026 removed entries (two Hong Kong addresses and one entity listed under Turkey, both on 2026-08-24) and added none, and BIS Federal Register documents since 2025-01-20 include no rule on de minimis, foreign direct product, deemed export, fundamental research or country-group changes.

timeline.event: BIS publishes two Entity List rules. One adds 12 entities (11 in China, one in Taiwan) for supercomputing and military-modernization links; the second adds 70 entries (68 unique entities), 42 of them under China and the rest mainly Pakistan, the UAE, South Africa and Iran. This link is the larger rule; the 12-entity rule is cited under sources.

BIS removes validated end-user authorizations for three China-based chip plants (Intel Dalian, Samsung China Semiconductor, SK hynix China), effective 2025-12-31, and estimates about 1,000 additional license applications a year as a result.

BIS adds 32 entries (30 unique entities) to the Entity List, 23 of them under China, citing military space, quantum, semiconductor-equipment diversion and circumvention concerns; also corrects 27 existing entries.
BIS interim final rule extends Entity List and similar end-user restrictions automatically to entities at least 50 percent owned by listed parties.

BIS adds 29 entries (26 entities and 3 addresses) to the Entity List, 19 of them under China including Hong Kong, mainly for supplying components to Iranian-linked drone programs; 9 Turkish entities and one UAE entity are also added.

BIS publishes a one-year suspension of the affiliates rule, effective 2025-11-10 through 2026-11-09, after which the provisions resume unless extended. The White House fact sheet of 2025-11-01 on a U.S.-China arrangement listed the suspension among U.S. steps.

BIS rule revises license review for advanced computing chips (such as Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X class) to China and Macau from presumption of denial to case-by-case, subject to certification, a 50 percent cap relative to U.S. shipments, security and third-party testing conditions.

BIS final rule raises the endurance threshold for national security controls on drones from one hour to three hours and removes those controls on related software and technology for lesser drones, describing the change as supporting U.S. drone industry competitiveness; it finalizes a January 2026 interim final rule.

title: Tighten export controls on China and expand Entity List restrictions
